To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Mandarin speakers' learning of Cantonese tone contrasts is affected by their musical aptitude and pitch thresholds.
the perceptual learning in level tone identification but not discrimination was affected by musical and pitch aptitudes.
Mandarin listeners with higher musical and pitch thresholds showed an advantage in learning Cantonese level tones.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the issue of how the perceptual learning is modulated by the listeners' musical and speech-related abilities.
the individual variability in learning a new language and the underlying cognitive and perceptual mechanisms.
the effect of listeners' musical aptitude on learning a new language.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the perceptual learning advantage of higher musical aptitude in the level tone learning of speakers of a contour tonal language may be due to the interaction of their musical aptitude and their prior experience in a tonal language.
musical and pitch aptitudes are important predictors of perceptual learning of tone contrasts, regardless of the listeners' language experience.
the perceptual learning advantage of listeners with higher musical and pitch abilities is not limited to the learning of tonal contrasts, but also extends to the learning of level tone systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the perceptual learning for Cantonese level tones by Mandarin listeners is facilitated by their musical and speech pitch aptitude.
musical and pitch aptitudes are associated with a more accurate perception and learning of level tone categories in Cantonese by Mandarin listeners.
musical and pitch aptitudes are important predictors of learning of level tones in listeners with experience of a tonality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effect of musical and pitch aptitudes should be considered in the design of training materials and in the assessment of perceptual learning.
listeners' musical and speech pitch aptitude are crucial for their perceptual learning of lexical tones in the absence of language-specific cues.
individual variability in the learning of tone categories is not only due to the listeners' experience of tonal or non-tonal language, but also to their musical and pitch abilities.
